an1.198:1.1: He was slow of understanding, rejected even by his brother, but then, supported by the Buddha, he achieved mastery ([thag10.4]()). The younger brother of Mahāpanthaka, he is praised at [ud5.10](), and give effective instruction to the nuns at [pli-tv-bu-vb-pc22:1.1]().
an1.199:1.1: “Evolution of heart” (_cetovivaṭṭa_) and “evolution of perception” (_saññāvivaṭṭa_) are obscure terms. Perhaps “evolution of heart” refers to Cūḷapanthaka’s remarkable transformation. The late canonical Paṭisambhidamagga, on the other hand, explains “evolution of heart” as wisdom regarding manifoldness, perhaps in reference to Cūḷapanthaka’s creating a thousand mind-made bodies, and  “evolution of perception” as wisdom regarding “rushing upon” (_adhipatattā_), perhaps in reference to Mahāpanthaka’s headlong rush to awakening ([ps1.0:44.1]()).
an1.200:1.1: His verses are at [thag8.3](), where tells of undertaking the resolve to not sit down until awakened.
an1.201:1.1: It seems Subhūti’s support of his fellow monk Saddha ([an11.14]()) was why he was foremost in non-strife declared the foremost in living without strife ([mn139:14.3](); he was additionally praised as worthy of donations. Subhūti’s meditation is praised at [ud6.7](), and his verse opens the Theragāthā at [thag1.1]().
an1.203:1.1: His verses are at [thag14.1](), and an isolated one at [thag1.42]().
